pr_title: Terraform test: Execute eligible test runs in parallel
pr_body:
<!--

Describe in detail the changes you are proposing, and the rationale.

See the contributing guide:

https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md

-->

<!--

Link all GitHub issues fixed by this PR, and add references to prior
related PRs.

-->

Fixes #34180

This PR introduces a graph-based execution model into the terraform test framework. With this model, test runs are able to execute in parallel. However, the rules for executing 2 runs in parallel must be fulfilled. Both runs must not share the same state, and there must be no interdependency between them.
The PR also introduces a new "test" block to test files. The block can be used to annotate the file's runs as candidates for parallelism. Each individual run block can however also set this attribute.
For now, the execution of a test run is split between the `Execute` method of the NodeTestRun, and the graph walk callback itself. Eventually, all logic should be moved into the `Execute` method.

-->

issue_context.title: Terraform Test: add the ability to run tests in parallel
issue_context.body:
### Terraform Version

```shell
Terraform v1.6.3
```


### Use Cases

In order to speed up the testing process, we would like to have the ability to run all the tests in parallel (which are not depended on each other) 

### Attempted Solutions

We tried to split our test into multiple testing files, but it seems the test still runs one by one and not in parallel 

### Proposal

Add the ability to run test in parallel

### References

_No response_
comments: Thanks for this feature request! If you are viewing this issue and would like to indicate your interest, please use the 👍 reaction on the issue description to upvote this issue. We also welcome additional use case descriptions. Thanks again!
Hey @ron-matsliah, the Terraform team is doing research into this problem, and I'd love to chat to learn more. Please reach out to me oismail@hashicorp.com and we can schedule a time to chat!
This feature will be super useful if I have to test a "heavy" module like RDS, I want to run provision multiple database instances with different engines in parallel .

Hey @sleepwithcoffee and @brettcurtis, I'm on the Terraform team and I'm doing research on this problem. I would love to learn more about your use cases! Please reach out to me [garvitarai@hashicorp.com](mailto:garvitarai@hashicorp.com) and we can schedule a time to chat!

Our team is very interested in this feature, it is a must have for our dev team to develop a terraform provider for our API product and we are seriously considering developping some other consumption channel for our product instead (like an ansible module).
If you have a way for a developper to run tests on their local machine in parallel, we are intrested.
For the CI pipelibe we use gitlab-ci parellel matrix to workaround this but we have no easy solution for local run

@garvitarai1 - Our use case is straight forward, we only use `test` for our child module development. Recently we switched to the mock provider for better or worse and don't have the need to run tests in parallel anymore since the mock tests are fast. We've accepted the tradeoff of tests not building real infrastructure.

A useful side effect here (though one that might create subtle differences in behavior) would be that presumably each block designated to run in parallel would essentially be sandboxed, i.e., the plan / apply / destroy would likely be within each run block, and / or there would have to be some kind of outer container for a group of `run` blocks to be within a single parallel test?

For plan only or mock provider tests, I'd think parallelism should be relatively easy / safe, and the isolation probably providing some benefits (see #35813 for some discussion on that) though the speed gains might be more modest.

In a lot of languages, you can specify which tests are safe to run in parallel (e.g., `t.Parallel()` in go) -- this might be a good way to still allow people to create tests that do need to run serially. like `run_parallel {}` (vs `run {}`) or `run { parallel = true }` maybe?

review_comments: We could probably just let whoever creates the runner also creates the semaphore directly since that's all the Concurrency is doing?
I think it's fine for the caller to just give us the concurrency value, and whether we use a semaphore or some other concurrency mechanism, is entirely an implementation detail.

So I think in the future, we'd want the actual run execution to happen in this function right? Like, ideally the whole execution of the nodes would happen in here. I think we can leave this as is for now, to keep the initial PR more contained, but perhaps you could leave a little TODO here that documents eventually we want to move more of the test run execution into the graph.
Yeah That's the plan. Thanks, I will leave a TODO comment.

Can we leave a comment here that clarifies exactly what is safe or not safe to do to this configuration. While we do take a copy of it, we don't copy any pointer fields within it so there is still data shared across all the run blocks. Just a little comment that states this, and tells people to be careful about exactly what they're editing would be great.
The need for such reset has been eliminated by creating a copy of the variables and provider config for each run

I've made a note of this elsewhere, but perhaps leave a comment here that explicitly documents this execute function isn't actually executing the tests but simply preparing the node for execution, so we'll slowly port more functionality over to the graph as we need it?
